title: Destructive confirmation cancel still submits forms
description:
During browser QA, destructive forms with data-sendword-confirm call window.confirm but still submit when confirm returns false.

Script repro: script editor rendered data-sendword-confirm="Delete qa-delete-confirm.sh?" and /static/js/sendword.js was present. Instrumenting window.confirm to record the message and return false still allowed DELETE SCRIPT to navigate to /scripts?success=Script+deleted.

User repro: Users page delete form called window.confirm with "Delete user qa-second@example.com?" and return false still allowed navigation to /admin/users?success=User+deleted.

Expected: cancelling the confirmation prevents form submission and leaves the user on the current page.
Actual: the confirmation is called but a false result does not stop deletion.

Likely area: static/js/sendword.js initFormConfirm submit/click cancellation behavior.
close_reason: Fixed and browser-retested

comments.author: nambiar
comments.text: Fixed in static/js/sendword.js by running the destructive submit confirmation listener in capture phase and stopping immediate propagation when cancelled, so HTMX boosted forms never submit after confirm=false. Regression: direnv exec . cargo test sendword_script_confirm_handler_runs_before_htmx_boosted_submit. Browser retest: full reload to rebuilt JS, script delete cancel captured 'Delete qaconfirmfixed2.sh?' with no network requests and row/editor remained; user delete cancel captured 'Delete user qa-confirm-fixed@example.com?' with no network requests and row remained. Accepting each delete then removed the disposable fixture.

title: Bound or stream regex log masking
description: Final migration review noted that regex-based live SSE masking now buffers all output until flush to avoid split-match leaks. This is security-conservative but long-running commands with regex masking lose live streaming and can accumulate unbounded memory. Follow up with a bounded-buffer design, documented behavior, or a streaming-safe regex masking strategy.
close_reason: Fixed live log masking behavior. Env-var masks stream with bounded tail reads and terminal backlog drain; regex masks defer live output and emit full masked logs at terminal to avoid boundary leaks. Verified with targeted SSE/log-tail tests, full cargo test --locked, and separate simplification/security/performance reviews.
